name: PDF.js text content transforms
what_it_is: PDF.js APIs and layout code for extracting page text runs and projecting their PDF-space transforms into a rendered page viewport. TextContent items expose strings, direction, transform, width, height, font name, and end-of-line hints, but not guaranteed per-glyph boxes.
render_model: Hybrid: getTextContent returns structured text runs; PageViewport maps PDF coordinates to viewport coordinates; TextLayer creates positioned and scaled DOM spans over the canvas.
annotation_support: Geometry source only for this use case. It can support an application-owned SVG/DOM overlay, but getTextContent itself does not create or persist annotations.
coordinate_space: TextItem.transform describes a text run in PDF-derived coordinates. PageViewport applies view box, userUnit, scale, rotation, offsets, and the Y-axis flip. Jevsume should normalize resulting top-left viewport rectangles to page fractions for its overlay and optionally retain PDF user-space rectangles for interoperability.
desktop_fit: Strong: render the PDF.js TextLayer from the same TextContent used to build an extraction ledger, translate Jev UTF-16 intervals to text-node intervals, and use DOM Range client rectangles for precise visual sub-ranges.
mobile_fit: Good: normalized page rectangles are independent of CSS size and can be projected onto responsive pages. Text layers for off-screen pages should be virtualized to control DOM and memory cost.
overlay_chat_fit: Strong: one finding can resolve to multiple normalized PageBox regions, with a separate normalized pin and thread trigger rendered in a sibling overlay above the page.
license: Apache License 2.0 as part of Mozilla PDF.js.
already_in_repo: Yes. pdfjs-dist is already used by src/lib/extract.ts, but current extraction discards TextItems after joining every item with a synthetic space and every page with a newline; it does not retain an offset-to-item ledger or geometry.
risks: TextItem boundaries are heuristic and are not words or glyphs; proportional fonts, ligatures, combining marks, RTL or vertical writing, and rotations make equal-width character interpolation approximate. Current synthetic separators do not correspond to PDF geometry. Scanned PDFs may have no text layer.
recommendation: use — retain TextContent and an exact extraction ledger, prefer TextLayer DOM Range rectangles for partial runs, normalize boxes to page space, and mark run-level interpolation as approximate.
uncertain: The exact Jev offset unit is inferred to be JavaScript UTF-16 code units from current String.slice usage; this should be made an explicit API contract.
DOM Range rectangles need fixture testing against pdfjs-dist 6.3.289 for ligatures, RTL, vertical text, and rotated pages.
A future PDF.js upgrade may change text-run segmentation or normalization, so anchors must be tied to an extraction-policy and document revision.
